title: fix(layout): a nav ancestor's gates reach its whole subtree, and a group does not outlive its children
body:
Fixes #10119

**Clause-②: no.** Derived from the diff: it NARROWS what renders and adds a module-private helper. No exported signature moves (`NavigationRenderer`'s props, `hasVisibleNavigationItems`' signature and `NavigationVisibilityOptions` are unchanged), no accept set is relaxed, no published surface widens.

**Clause-②-correction** — the claim comment on this card (comment id `5751359491`) deliberately carried no `Clause-②:` line, because the value is declared from the diff and there was no diff. The line above is that declaration; this is not a second `Claim:`.

---

## 1. The card's headline does not reproduce on today's `main` — measured, with a lit control

The card reports that an app nav item's `visible` CEL predicate is "authored, validated, persisted, and served to the browser intact — and then ignored". Re-derived here rather than relayed, and it is **no longer true**.

The reading that counts is a **comparison**, not an absence: the card's own predicate, in the shape the server serves it, run against **two sessions in one run**, with the `true` leg lit so the `false` leg's absence means something.

| session | `positions` | the card's predicate | leaf `Secret` | group `Admin Only` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Mia | `demo_member` | `false` | absent | absent |
| Otto | `other_team` | `true` | present | present |

`evaluateVisibility` routes the served envelope to the CEL engine and `NavigationRenderer` applies it per item. The behaviour the card asks for landed in `@object-ui/layout` / `@object-ui/app-shell` **17.1.0** — the release note for it is the one that begins "Nav gating fields finally gate" — while the card was filed against a Console build served alongside `@objectstack/*` 17.2.0, which is versioned on its own cadence.

⇒ this PR does **not** re-fix that. The ablation below shows it: with the fix reverted, the five cells describing the headline stay **green**.

## 2. What IS still broken — two other paths into the same subtree

The card's repro carries a predicate on **both a group and its leaf**, which is exactly where the remaining defect lives. Both of these reproduce on `main` and are fixed here.

**(a) A pinned descendant escaped its hidden ancestor.** The Favorites section collects pinned entries by walking `children`, and that walk asked nothing about the node it descended through. So an author could gate a group with `visible`, watch the group leave the tree, and still find a pinned entry from inside it rendered under Favorites — the predicate evaluated, answered `false`, and changed nothing the excluded user could see. That is the authoring-trap shape the card is about, one level down. `requiredPermissions` and the `requiresObject` / `requiresService` gates leaked by the same route, because the collection applied **none** of them; fixing only `visible` would have left the identical trap on the gate the card itself calls the better one. Reachable in the shipped Console: `UnifiedSidebar` — the sidebar `ConsoleLayout` mounts — passes `enablePinning` and restores pins from persisted state.

**(b) A group whose children were all hidden rendered as an empty husk.** Its own label still rendered as a disclosure that opens onto nothing. That also made a documented invariant false: `hasVisibleNavigationItems` — the predicate the area switcher elects areas by — already scores such a group as contributing nothing, and its docblock claims it "can never disagree with the rendered navigation". It did disagree.

## 3. The existing evaluator was found and reused — no second one was written

Named by symbol, as asked:

- **`evaluateVisibility`** (`@object-ui/app-shell`'s `ExpressionProvider`) — the shipped predicate evaluator. It handles literals and delegates everything else to `ExpressionEvaluator.evaluateCondition`, which routes CEL envelopes to the canonical `@objectstack/formula` engine. It is the same function the per-action capability gates and `RecordFormPage`'s field gates run through. **Called, not copied.**
- **`buildExpressionUser`** — the session-to-`current_user` normaliser that puts `positions` in scope, which is what the card's predicate names.
- **`hasVisibleNavigationItems`** (`@object-ui/layout`) — the existing derived-visibility predicate. Fix (b) calls **this**, rather than asking a new question about children.

The one thing added is `passesNavItemGuards`, and it is a **de-duplication, not a new evaluator**: the per-item guard sequence was written out twice (in `NavigationItemRenderer` and in `hasVisibleNavigationItems`) and omitted once (in the Favorites collection) — which is precisely how the two defects above arose. The three callers now share one statement instead of agreeing about it.

## 4. The nesting rule, settled

- **A group whose own predicate is `false`** ⇒ the group and its entire subtree are absent, **on every path the shell surfaces them**, the Favorites section included. An author who gates a group has gated its contents; a descendant escaping through a pin re-creates the trap.
- **A group whose children are all hidden** ⇒ the group is absent too. A labelled disclosure that opens onto nothing is a dead affordance, and the area derivation already scored it as nothing. A group authored with no children at all derives the same way, as it already did for area election.

Net effect: the sidebar and the area switcher can no longer disagree about what a user can reach, because one statement decides both.

## 5. Failure direction: FAIL-OPEN, chosen deliberately and pinned

A predicate that cannot be evaluated — malformed, missing session data, evaluator unavailable — **renders the entry**.

- It is this tier's already-ruled policy; `evaluateVisibility`'s own comment states it as "FAIL-OPEN IS UNCHANGED, deliberately", and reversing it is a behaviour change this card does not carry a mandate for.
- **Hiding a nav entry is presentation, not authorization.** The server still enforces object and record permissions on every route the entry would have led to, so "show on error" leaks an entry the server still refuses — not data. "Hide on error" would silently delete a user's navigation, with no diagnostic and nothing to report.
- The unresolvable-predicate diagnostic still fires and still names the predicate source, so a fault is loud rather than silent.

⛔ Nothing server-side is removed, weakened or "optimised away" on the strength of this gate, and this is **not** a security fix. A user who types the URL directly gets exactly the answer they get today.

## 6. Pins

All in one new file — `navItemVisibleEvaluated.test.tsx` in `@object-ui/app-shell`'s layout tests — which mounts the shipped chain: the real `ExpressionProvider`, the real evaluator built from a real session bag, and the real `NavigationRenderer`, wired with the same one-liner `UnifiedSidebar` and `AppSidebar` use.

1. Fails before, passes after — a leaf whose predicate is `false` is absent and the `true` one is present, both legs in one run against the same shell.
2. The nesting rule: a group with a `false` predicate takes its subtree with it, and a group whose children are all hidden leaves no husk.
3. A pinned descendant does not escape its hidden ancestor into Favorites.
4. The failure-direction pin: an unevaluable predicate renders, for both sessions.
5. A control: an item with **no** `visible` key renders identically for both sessions.

## 7. Reverse verification

The fix was committed first, then reverted on disk from the pinned base commit (proof that the mutation landed: the `passesNavItemGuards` marker count went 4 to 0), the pin was run, and the file was restored from `HEAD` and confirmed byte-identical by blob hash with an empty `git diff HEAD`.

Ablated result — **the predicted direction, and it separates the two claims cleanly**:

```
× a group whose children are ALL hidden leaves no empty husk behind
× a PINNED descendant does not escape its hidden ancestor into Favorites
  Tests  2 failed | 5 passed (7)
```

The five that stay green are the headline the card reported. The two that go red are what this PR actually fixes.

## 8. Checks on this head

Head is a merge of `origin/main` (merged, never rebased) taken after the last code change.

| check | result |
|:--|:--|
| `vitest run packages/layout/` | **22 files, 224 tests, all passing** |
| `vitest run packages/app-shell/` | **742 of 743 files, 7336 tests passing**, 1 failure — see below |
| pin, on the merged head | 7 passing |
| `type-check` — `@object-ui/layout` | passing |
| `type-check` — `@object-ui/app-shell` | passing |
| `pnpm lint` (repo-wide, 47 tasks) | passing, 0 errors |
| `check:control-bytes` | passing |
| `check:new-line-citations` | 0 new |
| changeset presence / no-major / claims / pending literals | passing |
| governed-surface guard | NOT GOVERNED, 3 paths checked |

**The one failure, named rather than swept up.** `AppContent.inaccessibleAppStrand.test.tsx` trips the repo's network-escape guard on `/api/v1/meta`, `/api/v1/meta/package` and `/api/v1/meta/diagnostics`. It is **not attributable to this change** and it is not claimed as pre-existing either — here is what was and was not measured:

- It **passes in isolation on this branch** and **passes in isolation at the base commit** — both measured, both exit 0.
- The escaping reads are app metadata; this diff adds, removes and reorders no fetch, and touches one file in `@object-ui/layout` while the failing fixture is in `app-shell`'s console tests and exercises neither nav groups nor pinned favorites.
- The guard's own text describes this class: a component issuing a read **after the test body returns**, whose socket the guard attributes to whichever test is running when it lands — which is why it surfaces only under full-suite load.
- **NOT MEASURED: the same full-package suite at the base commit under load.** That control was started and had not returned a verdict when this PR was opened; CI runs the full suite on both sides and settles it.

## Acceptance notes

Noted while working here, **not filed** and not fixed — out of this card's scope:

- `NavigationItem.visible` is declared `boolean | string`, while the transport actually hands the gate a `{ dialect, source }` envelope, so every fixture must cast to describe what production sends. This is a **known and deliberate** divergence — the declaration says so in its own docblock and a spec-derived-unions pin holds it in place — so it is recorded here rather than raised as a finding. Carrier for it: any future change to that declaration.
